result.overall: The Court allowed Mr. Senadheerage's application for judicial review, finding the RAD's decision unreasonable due to unsupported implausibility findings and an improper approach to corroboration, and remitted the matter for redetermination.

themes.name: Implausibility Findings
themes.summary: The Court found the RAD's implausibility findings were speculative and lacked a firm evidentiary basis, making them unreasonable.

themes.name: Requirement for Corroboration
themes.summary: The Court clarified the legal framework for requiring corroboration in refugee claims, emphasizing that there is no general requirement and that reasons must be given for demanding it.

themes.name: Rejection of Corroborating Evidence
themes.summary: The Court found the RAD's rejection of certain corroborating evidence reasonable, but noted the omission of a friend's letter contributed to the overall unreasonableness of the decision.

themes.name: Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) Analysis
themes.summary: The Court held the RAD improperly conflated the IFA analysis with its persecution findings, failing to assume a well-founded fear as required.

themes.name: Standard of Review and Reasonableness
themes.summary: The Court applied the reasonableness standard under Vavilov, emphasizing the need for a rational chain of analysis and compliance with legal constraints.

themes.name: Remedy and Redetermination
themes.summary: The Court ordered the matter remitted for redetermination due to the cumulative unreasonableness of the RAD's decision.

arguments.quote: the RAD erred in finding his story implausible, in rejecting his corroborative evidence and in requiring additional corroboration.
arguments.claim: The RAD erred by making implausibility findings, rejecting corroborative evidence, and improperly requiring additional corroboration.

arguments.quote: the RAD found that there was insufficient evidence that either the CID or the businessman’s thugs had any remaining interest in harming Mr. Senadheerage.
arguments.claim: There was insufficient evidence that the CID or the businessman’s thugs had any remaining interest in harming Mr. Senadheerage.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the implausibility findings speculative and unsupported.

arguments.quote: The RAD also confirmed the RPD’s analysis with respect to the IFA.
arguments.claim: The IFA finding was valid and confirmed the RPD's analysis.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the IFA analysis improperly conflated with persecution findings.

arguments.quote: the RAD stated that if they still had interest in Mr. Senadheerage, the CID and the thugs would have looked for members of his family and, in the case of the CID, friends and co-workers.
arguments.claim: If the CID or thugs still had interest, they would have sought out family, friends, or co-workers, so their lack of action shows no ongoing interest.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found this was speculative and not based on evidence.

arguments.quote: the RAD found that it was illogical that the CID would have gone to Mr. Senadheerage’s house in February 2018, as they would have known that he had left the country.
arguments.claim: It was illogical for the CID to visit the house in 2018, as they would have known he left the country.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found no evidence for this inference; it was speculative.

arguments.quote: the RAD found that Mr. Senadheerage failed to provide any documentary evidence supporting his testimony regarding the death threats the businessman made against him, which were relayed to him by a co-worker.
arguments.claim: Mr. Senadheerage failed to provide documentary evidence of the death threats relayed by a co-worker, so this aspect of his claim was uncorroborated.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the RAD did not justify why corroboration was required or consider reasonable explanations for its absence.
arguments.quote_snapped: Senadheerage failed to provide any documentary evidence supporting his testimony regarding the death threats the businessman made against him, which were relayed to him by a co-worker.

arguments.quote: he failed to provide a letter or an affidavit from his mother, with whom he still has contact, even though his mother is his only source of information with respect to significant events
arguments.claim: Mr. Senadheerage failed to provide a letter or affidavit from his mother, his only source for key events, so those events were uncorroborated.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the RAD did not give him a chance to explain the absence or justify the need for corroboration.

arguments.quote: the Minister, however, argues that the RAD’s IFA finding stands independently of its conclusion regarding Mr. Senadheerage’s lack of a well-founded fear of persecution.
arguments.claim: The IFA finding is independent and sufficient to uphold the RAD's decision even if the persecution analysis was flawed.
arguments.outcome_note: Court found the IFA analysis was tainted by the same errors as the persecution analysis.

holdings.quote: the standard of review is reasonableness: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov].
holdings.statement: The standard of review for immigration and refugee matters is reasonableness under Vavilov.

holdings.quote: the decision itself must be justified, not only justifiable. Thus, it must exhibit a rational chain of analysis that complies with the legal constraints bearing on the decision-maker: Vavilov, at paragraphs 102-107.
holdings.statement: A decision must be justified with a rational chain of analysis and comply with legal constraints, not merely be justifiable.

holdings.quote: I find that this aspect of the RAD’s decision is unreasonable.
holdings.statement: The RAD's implausibility findings were unreasonable because they were speculative and unsupported by evidence.

holdings.quote: I am unable to discern a rational chain of reasoning in the decision.
holdings.statement: The RAD's approach to corroboration was unreasonable and lacked a rational chain of reasoning.

holdings.quote: a decision-maker can only require corroborative evidence if: The decision-maker clearly sets out an independent reason for requiring corroboration, such as doubts regarding the applicant’s credibility, implausibility of the applicant’s testimony or the fact that a large portion of the claim is based on hearsay; The evidence could reasonably be expected to be available and, after being given an opportunity to do so, the applicant failed to provide a reasonable explanation for not obtaining it.
holdings.statement: A decision-maker may require corroboration only if there is an independent reason and the evidence could reasonably be expected to be available, with an opportunity for explanation.

holdings.quote: I find that some aspects of the RAD’s analysis with respect to corroboration are unreasonable.
holdings.statement: The RAD's analysis regarding the requirement for corroboration was unreasonable.

holdings.quote: I am unable to agree with him. The RAD analyzed that evidence and provided reasons for giving it little weight.
holdings.statement: The RAD's rejection of the newspaper article and lawyer's letter was reasonable.

holdings.quote: Its failure to do so may not, alone, have rendered its decision unreasonable. Nonetheless, it contributes to the decision’s overall unreasonableness.
holdings.statement: The RAD's omission to address the friend's letter contributed to the overall unreasonableness of the decision.

holdings.quote: the RAD’s analysis of the evidence is flawed in many respects.
holdings.statement: The RAD's analysis of the evidence was flawed and unreasonable overall.

holdings.quote: the RAD confused the two issues, at least in significant part.
holdings.statement: The RAD improperly conflated the IFA analysis with the persecution analysis.

holdings.quote: I am, however, unable to say that it would have come to the same conclusion had it not made the error identified above. Thus, I cannot sustain the decision on the basis of the IFA finding.
holdings.statement: The IFA finding cannot be sustained due to the errors in the persecution analysis.

holdings.quote: the application for judicial review will be allowed and the matter will be sent back for redetermination.
holdings.statement: The application for judicial review is allowed and the matter is remitted for redetermination.

rebuttals.quote: The findings appear to be based on the RAD’s own views of what is likely or unlikely. In doing so, however, the RAD did not consider the distinction between plausibility and likelihood, which is at the core of cases such as Valtchev and Al Dya.
rebuttals.point: Implausibility findings based on what the RAD thought likely or unlikely.
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD failed to distinguish plausibility from likelihood and based its findings on speculation, not evidence.

rebuttals.quote: There is, however, no evidence providing a reasonable basis for an inference in this regard.
rebuttals.point: The CID and thugs would have known Mr. Senadheerage left the country, so visits were implausible.
rebuttals.court_answer: There was no evidence to support this inference; the finding was speculative.

rebuttals.quote: The RAD did not make any explicit negative credibility findings. It did not follow the legal framework outlined above.
rebuttals.point: RAD required corroboration due to lack of credibility or implausibility.
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD did not make explicit credibility findings or follow the required legal framework for corroboration.

rebuttals.quote: I am, however, unable to say that it would have come to the same conclusion had it not made the error identified above. Thus, I cannot sustain the decision on the basis of the IFA finding.
rebuttals.point: IFA finding stands independently and supports dismissal regardless of errors in persecution analysis.
rebuttals.court_answer: The IFA analysis was tainted by the same errors and cannot independently support the decision.

authorities.quote: the standard of review is reasonableness: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 [Vavilov].
authorities.authority: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
authorities.why: Sets the standard of review and the requirement for a rational chain of analysis.

authorities.quote: Such a finding may be made only in the “clearest of cases:” Valtchev v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2001 FCT 776 [Valtchev]
authorities.authority: Valtchev v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2001 FCT 776
authorities.why: Establishes the high threshold for implausibility findings.

authorities.quote: the unusual or improbable does occur, and that it is unreasonable to reject evidence as not credible simply because the events it describes are unusual: Al Dya, at paragraph 35.
authorities.authority: Al Dya v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2020 FC 901
authorities.why: Clarifies that unusual events are not inherently implausible.

authorities.quote: There is no general requirement for corroboration and a panel errs if it makes an adverse credibility finding on the basis of the absence of corroborative evidence alone: Chen v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2019 FC 162 at paragraph 28.
authorities.authority: Chen v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2019 FC 162
authorities.why: Confirms there is no general requirement for corroboration.

authorities.quote: When an applicant swears to the truth of certain allegations, this creates a presumption that those allegations are true unless there be reason to doubt their truthfulness.
authorities.authority: Maldonado v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1980] 2 FC 302 (CA)
authorities.why: Establishes the presumption of truthfulness for sworn testimony.

authorities.quote: Corroborative evidence was only required if the RAD had (1) reason to doubt the Applicants’ claim and (2) the corroborating evidence could reasonably be expected to be available […].
authorities.authority: Horvath v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2018 CF 147
authorities.why: Sets out the two-step approach for requiring corroboration.

authorities.quote: when corroborative evidence should reasonably be available to establish the essential elements of a refugee protection claim and there is no reasonable explanation for its absence, the administrative decision maker may draw a negative inference
authorities.authority: Fatoye v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2020 FC 456
authorities.why: Describes the exception where corroboration may be required if evidence should reasonably be available.
